Resolution approving a First Amendment to Agreement for Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals between the City of Tampa and Life Extension Clinics, Inc. dba Life Scan Wellness Centers, with an escalation in pricing and revised scheduling, to provide for an annual renewal of the agreement in the estimated amount of $227,145 for use by the Human Resources & Talent Development Department/Risk & Insurance Division and the Tampa Police Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said First Amendment to Agreement for Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-25960
Resolution approving a First Amendment to Agreement for Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals between the City of Tampa and Life Extension Clinics, Inc. dba Life Scan Wellness Centers, with an escalation in pricing and revised scheduling, to provide for an annual renewal of the agreement in the estimated amount of $227,145 for use by the Human Resources & Talent Development Department/Risk & Insurance Division and the Tampa Police Department; authorizing the Mayor to execute said First Amendment to Agreement for Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
It is recommended that the City of Tampa renew its existing agreement with Life Extension Clinics, Inc. dba Life Scan Wellness Centers for the provision of Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals for use by the Human Resources Department for an additional one-year term. The existing agreement was made September 7, 2023. This agreement is in its initial term.

Life Extension Clinics, Inc. dba Life Scan Wellness Centers provides excellent service, quality of product and performance. The Human Resources Department has reviewed the price and feels that it is in the best interest of the City to renew the agreement for an additional one-year period. Life Extension Clinics, Inc. dba Life Scan Wellness Centers has agreed to renew Tampa Police Department (TPD) Voluntary Employee Prevention & Wellness Physicals with an escalation in pricing and revised scheduling.

SLBE participation goals were not prescribed in the solicitation because the scope did not meet required EBO parameters; however it did not preclude participation.

Equal Business Opportunity: Pursuant to the review by the Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Division, this one-year renewal contract is in compliance.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. NCA26-26398
Resolution approving the City of Tampa Gear Up Program agreement between the City of Tampa, Florida, and Hillsborough College to establish the Gear Up training program to provide up to fifty-one thousand six hundred and eighty-four dollars ($51,684) to Hillsborough College for up to four (4) scholarships to be awarded to students matriculating through the Hillsborough College Automotive Service Technology program to intern with the City Fleet Management Division; authorizing the execution thereof by the mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background: The City of Tampa (City) has established the Gear Up Training Program for students desiring to enter the skilled trades and technical professions for the purpose of training and providing a workforce for future in-demand careers.   The Gear Up program will assist successful applicants in obtaining the necessary training to become qualified for employment in specialized technical roles and other in-demand skilled professions for the City. Hillsborough College is the partner for the program and  provides accredited training for careers requiring certifications and vocational expertise in automotive service, repair and other specialized technical fields that meet operational needs of various city departments.  The City will select PSAV (Post-Secondary Adult Vocational) students to intern with the specified Department Management Division for the purpose of training while they matriculate through Hillsborough College accredited programs.  Students' tuition for the program will be covered while in the city's employ. Through this Agreement, the City will assist successful Gear Up applicants by providing Hillsborough College the value of up to four (4) scholarships in an amount for a total not to exceed Fifty-One Thousand Six-Hundred and Eighty-Four Dollars (51,684) total, to support the matriculation of the Gear Up participants.   It is necessary for the City and Hillsborough College to enter into an agreement to address their responsibilities under the Scholarship Program.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, approving additional expenditures within an existing standardization award between the City of Tampa and TSC-Jacobs Florida, LLC, for the purchase of Parts and Services for Hydro-Dyne Screening System in the estimated amount of $372,739 for a cumulative total expenditure of $422,739, for use by the Wastewater Department; authorizing the Director of Purchasing to purchase said property, supplies, materials or services; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The Wastewater Department has standardized replacement parts and services for the Hydro-Dyne screening system from TSC-Jacobs Florida, LLC.  Standardizing this equipment and these services ensures cost reduction, interoperability because of familiarity among staff, maintenance efficiency and reduced cost of inventory maintenance for parts and uninterrupted delivery of service, reduction of redundancies and costly expenditures for implementation of a new service.  It is recommended that the City purchase replacement parts and services for the Hydro-Dyne screening system.

Equal Business Opportunity: There was no EBO Participation as this purchase is being made under a standardization.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. INF26-26357
Resolution approving an Agreement for Design-Build initial services in the amount of $734,000 between the City of Tampa and Skanska USA Building, Inc. in connection with Contract 25-C-00022 K-Bar Park Design-Build; authorizing the Mayor of the City of Tampa To execute same; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 25-C-00022 K-Bar Park Design-Build a. Address of Project: Paddock View Drive, Tampa, FL 33647 b. Number of bidders/submitters: 8 c.    Names of bidders/submitters: • Bandes Construction Company, Inc.

• Kimmins Contracting Corp.

• Legacy Sports Construction LLC • LEMA Construction & Developers, Inc. (LEMA Construction, Inc.) • Phinazee Construction and Consulting Services, Inc.

• SCG Fields, LLC • Skanska USA Building, Inc.

• The A.D. Morgan Corporation d.    Dollar amount: $734,000.00 e. Why the awardee was selected: Selected via Consultants’ Competitive Negotiation Act Selection Committee

2. Contractor/Firm: Skanska USA Building, Inc.

3. Business Case: This agreement is for the Initial pre-construction services for the construction of a new neighborhood park facility for northeast Tampa neighborhoods .  There are few City park facilities in this area of the City, which has seen a lot of growth, and this park will help address that deficit.

4.    Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Skanska USA Building, Inc the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing 4 city-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: The park has already added significant tree count to the City within the last year.  The park design is anticipated to provide a natural, wooded buffer along several sides of the perimeter, provide significant open lawn and landscape areas for water infiltration and water quality enhancement, and provide habitat for gopher tortoise.

6. Community Engagement: the Parks and Recs Department will assist the Design Build Team communication efforts to ensure involvement and engagement of stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: K-Bar Ranch Park c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) •  365 consecutive calendar days from Initial Agreement NTP through the Completion of Pre-Construction.[SR1.1][MB1.2] •  The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background:
The Water Department rents out portable water meters to its customers. Due to the high cost of replacing a portable water meter, the Water Department requires a deposit. Customers are also required to pay a deposit whenever they open a new utility account. Any monies received in the form of a deposit requires earned interest to be paid to the customer.

This resolution appropriates interest earnings in the total amount of $100,000 to cover the costs of interest on portable meters and customer deposits.

agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. DEO26-23534
Resolution making certain changes in the budget of the City of Tampa for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026; approving the transfer, reallocation, and/or appropriation of $4,254,558 for all Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) Funds for fiscal year 2026 appropriation; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
During the review of the FY2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, a comment was received by a Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA) reviewer regarding the transfers from the Community Redevelopment Agency fiduciary funds to the General Fund.

"Reimbursements should not be displayed in the financial statements as transfers. The disclosure makes it appear as though reimbursements are reported as transfers.

Reimbursements should be treated as a reduction to the originally booked expense/expenditure and therefore would not be reported as an item in the external financial statements ". [GASB-S34:112b(2)].  The accounting department has updated their treatment of these particular transfers in the external financial statements for FY2025 and is now adjusting the transfers that have been made in FY2026.

Instead of recording services performed by the General Fund (primarily staff expenses) for the CRA as a revenue, the General Fund will record receiving reimbursement as a contra-expense (or negative expense).  The reason for this is to prevent the City's annual financials from recording the same expense twice:  once within the General Fund and again within the various CRA funds.  This has a neutral impact on both the financial standings/report for both entities.

CRA Director Cedric McCray brief the CRA Board during the July 2026 meeting on this topic.

SubjectOrdinance Amending Chapter 26.5
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
An Ordinance of the City of Tampa, Florida, deleting, In Its entirety, the City of 
Tampa Code of Ordinances, Articles I, II and III of Chapter 26.5, Equal 
Business Opportunity Program; adopting revised Articles I, II, and III of 
Chapter 26.5, renaming Equal Business Opportunity to Strategic Business 
Development; providing for severability; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
The Legislature of the State of Florida has, in Chapter 166, Florida Statutes, Municipalities, 
conferred upon local governments the authority to adopt regulations designed to promote the 
public health, safety, and general welfare of its citizenry.  Tampa City Council has determined 
that it is in the public interest to amend Articles I, II, and III of Chapter 26.5, Equal Business 
Opportunity Program, to promote efficient administration and update the provisions of the 
Strategic Business Development (f/k/a Equal Business Opportunity Program) to reflect 
current practices.

agendaItems.background: A strategic plan (Master Plan) provides a reasonable and attainable roadmap for current and future decision makers with prioritizing needs and developing a better understanding of legitimate first responder goals. It is the desire of City Council to formalize the process for presenting the respective Master Plans. The Mayor of the City of Tampa has drafted an Executive Order to clarify and provide greater structure to the process of creating a Master Plan. Tampa City Council will consider a Resolution for the same purposes as provided for in the Mayor’s Executive Order. And City Council has determined that enactment of this Ordinance will assure that it is put on notice of any changes to the Executive Order issued by the Mayor regarding the Master Plan.

SubjectAn ordinance of the City of Tampa, Florida requiring City Council to be 
provided notice of any changes to the E.O setting standards for triennial 
updates to the respective public safety master plans of the TPD and TFR.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
An ordinance of the City of Tampa, Florida requiring City Council to be 
provided notice of any changes to the Executive Order setting standards for 
triennial updates to the respective public safety master plans of the Tampa 
Police Department and Tampa Fire Rescue; repealing all ordinances or parts 
of ordinances in conflict therewith; providing for severability; providing an 
effective date.
BACKGROUND:
A strategic plan (Master Plan) provides a reasonable and attainable roadmap for current and 
future decision makers with prioritizing needs and developing a better understanding of 
legitimate first responder goals. It is the desire of City Council to formalize the process for 
presenting the respective Master Plans. The Mayor of the City of Tampa has drafted an 
Executive Order to clarify and provide greater structure to the process of creating a Master 
Plan. Tampa City Council will consider a Resolution for the same purposes as provided for in 
the Mayor’s Executive Order. And City Council has determined that enactment of this 
Ordinance will assure that it is put on notice of any changes to the Executive Order issued by 
the Mayor regarding the Master Plan.

agendaItems.background:
A resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, calling for public hearings on the proposed designation of a brownfield area for rehabilitation pursuant to Chapter 376, Florida Statutes, upon an application from ACE Fletcher LLC, c/o Aureate Development LLC, for property consisting of one parcel generally located Northeast of the intersection of North 46th Street and East Fletcher Avenue consisting of approximately 62 acres in the City of Tampa, Florida; providing for notice; providing an effective date.

The contamination identified in soil and groundwater is commonly associated with the application of pesticides consistent with the property’s former use as a golf course. ACE Fletcher LLC, c/o Aureate Development LLC, must continue site investigation and conduct remediation for the redevelopment project. The property will be redeveloped for public university purposes consistent with the 2020-2030 Campus Development Master Plan, as amended, and the 2nd Amendment to Campus Development Agreement dated January 2, 2026, between the City of Tampa and The University of South Florida Board of Trustees.

SubjectA resolution of the City of Tampa calling for two public hearings on the 
proposed Fletcher District Green Reuse Site Brownfield Area Designation.
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, calling for public hearings on the 
proposed designation of a brownfield area for rehabilitation pursuant to 
Chapter 376, Florida Statutes, upon an application from ACE Fletcher LLC, 
c/o Aureate Development LLC, for property consisting of one parcel generally 
located Northeast of the intersection of North 46th Street and East Fletcher 
Avenue consisting of approximately 62 acres in the City of Tampa, Florida; 
providing for notice; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
A resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, calling for public hearings on the proposed 
designation of a brownfield area for rehabilitation pursuant to Chapter 376, Florida Statutes, 
upon an application from ACE Fletcher LLC, c/o Aureate Development LLC, for property 
consisting of one parcel generally located Northeast of the intersection of North 46th Street 
and East Fletcher Avenue consisting of approximately 62 acres in the City of Tampa, Florida; 
providing for notice; providing an effective date. 
The contamination identified in soil and groundwater is commonly associated with the 
application of pesticides consistent with the property’s former use as a golf course. ACE 
Fletcher LLC, c/o Aureate Development LLC, must continue site investigation and conduct 
remediation for the redevelopment project. The property will be redeveloped for public 
university purposes consistent with the 2020-2030 Campus Development Master Plan, as 
amended, and the 2nd Amendment to Campus Development Agreement dated January 2, 
2026, between the City of Tampa and The University of South Florida Board of Trustees.

agendaItems.background:
The Yards at 40th and Lake is a proposed affordable housing development located on multiple parcels in the area bounded by East Lake Avenue, Lindell Avenue, North 39th Street, and North 40th Street in Tampa. The developer, The Yards at 40th and Lake, LLLP, plans to redevelop the site into a 96‑unit multifamily residential community. As part of the project, at least 10 percent of the units will be designated as affordable housing in accordance with Florida Statutes, supporting the City’s efforts to expand housing opportunities for income‑eligible residents.

The property is currently designated for Light Industrial use under the Comprehensive Plan and is zoned Industrial General. However, under Section 166.04151 of the Florida Statutes, the City has the authority to approve affordable housing developments on such sites without requiring a change to the underlying land use or zoning.

File No. E2026-8 CH 2, 14 & 16
(Ordinance being presented for first reading consideration) - An ordinance of the City of Tampa, Florida, relating to omitting any reference to firearms in deference to the preemption requirement of Florida Statute 790.33; making revisions to City of Tampa Code Chapter 14 (Offenses); repealing Section 14-111; Chapter 2 (Administration); amending Section 2-404; Chapter 16 (Parks and Recreation); amending Section 16-21 of Ordinances providing for severability; repealing all ordinances in conflict; providing for an effective date.
agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. E2026-8 CH 2, 14 & 16
(Ordinance being presented for first reading consideration) - An ordinance of the City of Tampa, Florida, relating to omitting any reference to firearms in deference to the preemption requirement of Florida Statute 790.33; making revisions to City of Tampa Code Chapter 14 (Offenses); repealing Section 14-111; Chapter 2 (Administration); amending Section 2-404; Chapter 16 (Parks and Recreation); amending Section 16-21 of Ordinances providing for severability; repealing all ordinances in conflict; providing for an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
Tampa Code Section 14-111, passed in 1989, makes it unlawful for any person to sell, offer for sale, give or have in his possession within the city any blank cartridge pistal or other like device made exclusively for the purpose of firing or discharging any blank cartridge, provided that this section shall not apply to the sale, possession or discharge of any pistol or other like device designed to use .22 caliber crimped blanks and/or .22 caliber tear gas cartridges.

Tampa Code Section 2-404(a)(1), passed in 2009, specifies that during the existence of a declared state of local emergency, the mayor may impose by executive order any or all of the following restrictions: Prohibit or regulate the purchase, sale, transfer or possession of explosives, combustibles, dangerous weapons of any kind (except firearms which may be restricted by F.S. § 870.044), or alcoholic beverages.

Tampa Code Section 16-21, passed in 2009, requires a facility rental application to indicate if (7) the applicant desires to carry, fire, or discharge any weapon, fireworks, or explosive of any kind.  By legislation enacted by the state during the 2011 legislative session, Florida Statute Section 790.33 has been amended effective October 1, 2011 to make clear that all regulation related to firearms and ammunition has been preempted to the state.

Florida Statute § 790.33 provides for penalties including a civil fine of up to $5,000 against local government officials for enacting or causing to be enforced any local ordinance or administrative rule or regulation related to firearms or ammunition.  The City of Tampa wishes to conform these Sections to changes in state law.

City Council has conducted duly noticed public hearings as required by law, at which hearings all parties in interest and citizens were afforded notice and the opportunity to be heard.

agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 24-C-09001; FY 24 Citywide Distribution Watermain Improvements Design-Build a. Dollar amount: $9,825,392.59 b. Why the awardee was selected: Selected Pursuant to FS 287.055 CCNA.

2. Contractor/Firm: Kimmins Contracting Corp.

3. Business Case: Project scope includes coordination and scheduling during the permitting and design phase, cost estimating, construction engineering and inspection (CEI), public relations, administering subcontracts and all related work required for a completed project.

Services will be provided under a task order contract for a guaranteed negotiated maximum price (GMP).

GMP 1 provided for construction of approximately, 2,760 linear feet of various sized water mains to be replaced/upgraded to be relocated along South Howard Avenue. Work also included arborist services, maintenance of traffic (MOT), site preparation, installation of water mains, roadway reconstruction, and landscape/irrigation restoration.

GMP 2 provides for construction of various sized water mains and service lines within the Wellswood East Neighborhood. The project area is bordered by Hillsborough Avenue to the north, N Boulevard to the east, N Armenia Avenue to the west and W. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr Blvd to the south.. Work includes replacing pipelines with diameters of 12-in or less as well as fire hydrants assemblies, meter sets, service laterals, valves and various fittings required for a complete and functioning system.

4.Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: The 17.4% subcontract goal for this contract was originally calculated and subsequently confirmed by the Goal Set Review Committee.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: Project provides for construction and public relations for various non-contiguous distribution water infrastructure improvements throughout the City’s water service area.

6. Community Engagement: The CAD Construction, Engineering and Inspection (CAD-CEI) team will assist the Contractor in the communication efforts to ensure transparency and integration of the stakeholders.

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design-Build project. A full-time City of Tampa Construction Inspector will be on-site during the project to ensure quality of construction.

b. Placemaking: N/A c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 309 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

Resolution approving the renewal of an award between the City of Tampa and Rogers Petroleum, Inc., based on current Port of Tampa, Florida average terminal rack prices published daily in Oil Price Information Services ("OPIS"), United Publications, for the furnishing of Fuel: Gasoline and Diesel (Bid Discount) (Re-Bid) in the estimated amount of $13,254,795.10 for use by the Logistics and Asset Management Department/Fleet Maintenance Division; authorizing the Director of Purchasing to purchase said property, supplies, materials or services; providing an effective date.

Memorandum from Ronald Carrion, Fleet Manager, transmitting additional information for said agenda item. (To be R/F)
agendaItems.background:
It is recommended that the City renews its existing award with Rogers Petroleum, Inc. for the provision of Fuel: Gasoline and Diesel (Bid Discount) (Re-Bid) for use by the Logistics and Asset Management Fleet Maintenance Division for an additional two-year term. The existing award was made on January 9, 2025. This award is in its original award term.

Rogers Petroleum, Inc. provides excellent service, quality of product and performance. The Logistics & Asset Management Fleet Maintenance Division has reviewed the prices and feels that it is in the best interest of the City to renew the award for an additional two -year period.

Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Office: Pursuant to the review by the Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Division, this one-year renewal contract is in compliance.

City of Tampa
Agenda Item Request
Department: Purchasing
Council Regular
Submittal Date:                        7/06/2026
Requested Meeting Date: 8/27/2026
Type of Request:                                                  Council Resolution
ContactMichele Neff 8132748636
SubjectReso approving the renewal of Rogers Petroleum, Inc. for Fuel: Gasoline and 
Diesel (Bid Discount) (Re-Bid) in the amount of $ 13,254,795.10 for use by 
Logistics and Asset Management Department/Fleet Maintenance Division
Resolution / 
Ordinance 
Title
A Resolution approving the renewal of an award between the City of Tampa 
and Rogers Petroleum, Inc., based on current Port of Tampa, Florida average 
terminal rack prices published daily in Oil Price Information Services ("OPIS"), 
United Publications, for the furnishing of Fuel: Gasoline and Diesel (Bid 
Discount) (Re-Bid) in the estimated amount of $13,254,795.10 for use by the 
Logistics and Asset Management Department/Fleet Maintenance Division; 
authorizing the Director of Purchasing to purchase said property, supplies, 
materials or services; providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
It is recommended that the City renews its existing award with Rogers Petroleum, Inc. for the 
provision of Fuel: Gasoline and Diesel (Bid Discount) (Re-Bid) for use by the Logistics and 
Asset Management Fleet Maintenance Division for an additional two-year term. The existing 
award was made on January 9, 2025. This award is in its original award term.
Rogers Petroleum, Inc. provides excellent service, quality of product and performance. The 
Logistics & Asset Management Fleet Maintenance Division has reviewed the prices and feels 
that it is in the best interest of the City to renew the award for an additional two -year period. 
Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Office: Pursuant to the review by the Equal Business 
Opportunity (EBO) Division, this one-year renewal contract is in compliance.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
This resolution renews an award between the City and Rogers Petroleum, Inc. for the 
furnishing of Fuel: Gasoline and Diesel (Bid Discount) (Re-Bid) in the estimated amount of 
$13,254,795.10, over a 24-month term, subject to annual appropriation, for use by various 
departments and shall be controlled by requisition.
PROJECTED COSTS: $5,522,831.29 FY2027 (Estimated Expenditures) controlled by 
requisition
$6,627,397.55 FY2028 (Estimated Expenditures) subject to annual appropriation, controlled 
by requisition

$1,104,566.26 FY2029 (Estimated Expenditures) subject to annual appropriation, controlled 
by requisition
